{{Short description|Mathematics competition in Hong Kong}}
{{Use dmy dates|date=January 2024}}
The '''Primary Mathematics World Contest''' ('''PMWC'''; {{zh|t=保良局小學數學世界邀請賽|s=保良局小学数学世界邀请赛|first=t,s}}) is an annual math competition for primary school students in [[Hong Kong]]. It was first held in 1997 and is sponsored by [[Po Leung Kuk]]. The competition has attracted teams from around the world.

==History==
The first Primary Mathematics World Contest (PMWC) was organised in 1997.<ref name="Dawn2018-03-31">{{cite news |date=2018-03-31 |title=International mathematics contests |url=https://www.dawn.com/news/1398088 |newspaper=[[Dawn (newspaper)|Dawn]] |accessdate=2024-01-26 |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20240126093050/https://www.dawn.com/news/1398088 |archivedate=2024-01-26 }}</ref> The sponsors of the competition are the charitable organisation [[Po Leung Kuk]], the public university [[Hong Kong Institute of Education]], and [[Panda Hotel]].<ref name="Hicap2007-07-18">{{cite news |last=Hicap |first=Jonathan M. |date=2007-07-18 |title=Pinoy kids reap HK top math awards |url=https://infoweb.newsbank.com/apps/news/document-view?p=WORLDNEWS&docref=news/11A748177AA09F08&f=basic |newspaper=[[The Manila Times]] |accessdate=2024-01-26 |archiveurl=https://archive.today/20240126103412/https://infoweb.newsbank.com/apps/news/document-view?p=WORLDNEWS&docref=news/11A748177AA09F08&f=basic |archivedate=2024-01-26 }}</ref> Competitions are held at the Panda Hotel, which is in the [[Tsuen Wan]] town of [[New Territories West]].<ref name="Hicap2007-07-18"/><ref name="Shukla2015-07-24">{{cite news |last=Shukla |first=Kavyanjali |date=2015-07-24 |title=Lucknow school represents India at Hong Kong cultural fest |url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/nri/citizen-journalists/citizen-journalists-reports/kavyanjali-shukla/lucknow-school-represents-india-at-hong-kong-cultural-fest/articleshow/48174799.cms |newspaper=[[The Times of India]] |accessdate=2024-01-26 |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20240126111300/https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/nri/citizen-journalists/citizen-journalists-reports/kavyanjali-shukla/lucknow-school-represents-india-at-hong-kong-cultural-fest/articleshow/48174799.cms |archivedate=2024-01-26 }}</ref>

==Format==
The event has an individual and a team competition. The individual contest's participants have 90 minutes to finish 15 math questions.<ref name="Macau2017-07-28">{{cite news |date=2017-07-28 |title=港數學賽澳奪團體冠軍 |trans-title=Hong Kong Mathematics Competition: Macau wins team championship |language=zh |url=http://macautimes.cc/news-cd.asp?id=26561 |newspaper={{ill|Macau Times|zh|澳門時報}} |accessdate=2024-01-26 |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20240126102411/http://macautimes.cc/news-cd.asp?id=26561 |archivedate=2024-01-26 }}</ref> The ratio of gold to silver to bronze medals is 1:2:3, and half of the participants receive medals. In 2016, a student who got all the questions right received gold medals, while students who got one question wrong received a silver medal.<ref name="Guo2016-07-18">{{cite news |last1=Guo |first1=Huiqiao 郭会桥 |last2=Shen |first2=Ao 沈翱 |date=2016-07-18 |title=图文：瞧 别人家的孩子真是不一般的牛 |trans-title=Picture and text: Look, other people’s children are really extraordinary. |language=zh |newspaper={{ill|Chutian Metropolis Daily|zh|楚天都市报}} }}</ref> In 2014, the cutoffs for bronze, silver, and gold were 10/15, 12/15, and 14/15 solves respectively. 

During the team competition, team members have 60 minutes to finish 10 math questions.<ref name="Macau2017-07-28" /> Each team has four people.<ref name="Guo2016-07-18" /> First, the four participants are given 8 questions, where they have about 10 minutes to skim through them and distribute the problems amongst themselves. They then individually work on the questions they've selected until time is up. It is not required for each participant to get exactly 2 of the 8 questions. Afterwards, they are no longer allowed to work on these 8 questions and must work on the last 2 questions together as a group.
